tools.name: get_supported
tools.description: The (x402Version, scheme, network) kinds and extensions this facilitator verifies and settles. Same answer as GET /supported.

tools.name: get_config
tools.description: Every settleable asset with its address, decimals, transfer method and EIP-712 domain values, plus the pricing model (gas at cost, plus a fee in basis points on the payment value when the asset has a USD price), the gas fallback and the free-credit allowances. Same answer as GET /api/config.

tools.name: get_health
tools.description: Whether the facilitator behind this host is answering. Same answer as GET /health.

tools.name: verify_payment
tools.description: Check a signed x402 payment against its requirements: signature, amount, balance and simulation. Moves no funds. Same answer as POST /verify, and it spends the same per-IP allowance.

tools.name: payment_status
tools.description: Whether a signed payment authorization has been used on chain, for a client whose settle reply was lost. findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "payment_status" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_payment · Private data: payment_status · Public sink: verify_payment.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_payment · Private data: payment_status · Public sink: verify_payment

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
